messages:
Payton: Hey team — after we pinned our account to model `open-embed-1024@2026-03-12` we started seeing returned embeddings with length 512. This broke our downstream similarity index.

Payton: Minimal repro: we call the embeddings endpoint with a single text. Before pin it was 1024, after pin it's 512. No other changes on our side.

Payton: curl example:
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"open-embed-1024","input":"test string","include_metadata":true}'
```

Payton: response snippet (post-pin):
```
{"object":"embedding","data":[{"embedding":[0.002,-0.12,...],"index":0}],"model":"open-embed-1024","vector_length":512}
```

Alex (Support): Thanks Payton — sorry about the break. Can you paste the full `request_id` from one failed call (we log it in headers) and confirm whether this happens for single-item requests or only batched requests?

Payton: request_id: req_20260312_8af3c2. Happens for single-item and batched payloads. We tested 1, 5, and 20 inputs — all returned 512. Also our historic embeddings (pre-pin) are 1024 so index errors are everywhere.

Mike (ML Eng): Noted. A few quick checks: 1) Which exact alias did you pin to? 2) Any custom quantization flag? 3) Is `include_metadata` required to reproduce?

Payton: We pinned via the console to alias `account:open-embed-1024:locked-20260312`. No custom quant flags set on our side. `include_metadata` = true in our example but we also see same result with `false`.

Alex (Support): I'm pulling the mapping for that alias now. One moment.

infra-bot: deployment event: variant `open-embed-512-quant` auto-synced to alias `open-embed-1024` during rollback reconciliation at 2026-03-12T03:22:11Z — triggered by model registry reconciliation job #mr-9921.

Mike (ML Eng): That log looks suspicious — sounds like the alias resolver picked a compatible runtime variant (512-quant) instead of the 1024 model. It may be a metadata collision in the registry: two variants share the same capability tag.

Mike (ML Eng): Quick repro I ran in staging reproduces the behavior when the alias points to `open-embed-512-quant`. The runtime returns vector_length=512 but still reports model name `open-embed-1024` in the response (weird mismatch).

Payton: Oh interesting — so the model label and actual vector size are inconsistent. That would explain why we saw `model: open-embed-1024` with 512 dims.

Sara (SRE): I'm kicking off a scoped rollback of the alias mapping and will pin a verified 1024 variant to the alias while we investigate registry reconciliation.

Sara (SRE): Action items: 1) rollback alias to verified `open-embed-1024-fp32@2026-02-25` (in progress), 2) run a registry integrity check to find other aliases with variant-tag collisions, 3) add an automated preflight that validates `vector_length` matches alias metadata on sync.

Alex (Support): Payton, once I confirm the rollback is complete can you re-run your failing request and paste the response header `x-request-id` back here so we can confirm?

Payton: I'll watch and re-test. Appreciate the quick response.

Mike (ML Eng): For long-term fix we'll: 1) patch reconciliation to prefer exact-dim matches for embeddings aliases, 2) add an alert when returned `vector_length` differs from alias metadata, 3) audit model registry tags. I'll open a ticket in our backlog and link it here.

Payton: Confirmed — after rollback our single-call response shows `vector_length":1024` and similarity index is happy again. request id: req_20260312_8af3c2 (same as before).

Alex (Support): Great — thanks for validating. I've escalated to Escalations team to follow up on the registry fix and you'll get a postmortem with timeline and root cause. Sorry again for the disruption. :pray:

Payton: Thanks everyone. A follow-up ask: can you provide a short recommended process for customers before pinning aliases to avoid this risk?
